qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: High capital intensity ($10B+ per fab shell) and leading-edge semiconductor physics (EUV, 1-gamma DRAM, G9 NAND, HBM3E/HBM4 packaging) restrict leading DRAM manufacturing to a 3-player oligopoly (Micron, Samsung, SK Hynix). However, memory bits are standardized JEDEC commodities lacking switching costs, leaving Micron as a price-taker subject to severe boom-bust cycles. Gross margins swing from negative (-8% in FY23) to peak (~40% in FY25). Primary erosion threats include cyclical overcapacity additions, aggressive capital expenditure by Korean peers, Chinese state-subsidized competition (CXMT, YMTC), and geopolitical restrictions in China.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & Commodity Price-Taker, REJECT). Micron participates in a 3-player DRAM and 5-player NAND oligopoly, but memory products remain standardized JEDEC commodities with zero customer switching costs. Micron lacks pricing power across the cycle, with average selling prices dictated by spot/contract market supply gluts and shortages. 10-year median ROIC is sub-hurdle at ~8.2%, swinging from deeply negative (-12.1% in FY23) to cyclical peaks (+14.5% in FY25). Massive ongoing capital expenditure requirements ($13.8B in FY25) to maintain node transitions (1-beta/1-gamma DRAM, high-layer 3D NAND, HBM3E/HBM4 packaging) structurally depress multi-cycle free cash flow conversion.
qualitative.evidence: Empirical financial record confirms chronic cyclicality and commodity price-taking behavior: (1) ROIC: 10-year median ROIC is ~8.2%, below the 12% Munger hurdle. ROIC collapsed to -12.1% in FY23 (industry trough) and 1.6% in FY24, rebounding to 14.5% in FY25 during the AI/HBM upcycle. (2) Revenue & Net Income: Revenue plunged from $30.8B in FY22 to $15.5B in FY23 with a net loss of -$5.83B, recovering to $25.1B in FY24 (net income $778M) and $37.38B in FY25 (GAAP net income $8.54B). (3) Free Cash Flow & Capex: Highly capital-intensive manufacturing treadmill. FY23 FCF burned -$6.12B, FY24 FCF was $121M, and in FY25, despite $8.54B net income, capex expanded to $13.80B, yielding only ~$1.67B in FCF (<20% conversion). (4) Pricing Power: No structural pricing power above inflation; ASPs fluctuate with spot memory market balances. High customer concentration among hyperscalers and PC/mobile OEMs who aggressively negotiate memory prices.
